• **Chapter 8: Internet and Web Services** forms a core module in the Class 7 DAV Hands-On in Computer / ICT curriculum, designed to build fundamental digital literacy.
• The chapter introduces students to the expansive digital ecosystem, moving beyond basic desktop computing to interconnected global networks.
• **Internet Definition:** The Internet is defined as a massive global system of interconnected computer networks that communicate using standardized communication protocols.
• **Network of Networks:** It links millions of private, public, academic, business, and government networks across local-to-global scopes.
• **Historical Roots:** The origins of the Internet trace back to **ARPANET** (Advanced Research Projects Agency Network), commissioned by the United States Department of Defense in the late 1960s.
• **ARPANET Significance:** ARPANET was the first network to implement packet switching, establishing the foundational architecture for modern internet communication.
• **World Wide Web (WWW):** Invented by **Tim Berners-Lee** in 1989, the WWW is a vast collection of interlinked multimedia documents accessed via the internet.
• **Internet vs. WWW Misconception:** Students must note that the Internet is the physical hardware infrastructure, whereas the Web is the software/information service running on top of that infrastructure.
• **ISP (Internet Service Provider):** An organization, such as Airtel, Jio, or BDSL, that provides individuals and businesses access to the Internet and related services.
• **Modem:** A hardware device—standing for Modulator-Demodulator—that converts digital computer signals into analog signals for transmission over telephone or cable lines, and vice versa.
• **Broadband Connectivity:** High-speed internet transmission characterized by wide bandwidth, allowing multiple communication channels simultaneously.
• **Wi-Fi Technology:** Wireless Fidelity enables electronic devices to connect to a wireless local area network (WLAN) using radio waves, typically utilizing 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz frequency bands.
• **Hotspot:** A physical location where people can access internet services, typically using Wi-Fi technology, via a wireless local area network managed by a router connected to an ISP.
• **Bandwidth:** The maximum rate of data transfer across a given path, measured in bits per second (bps), Kilobits per second (Kbps), Megabits per second (Mbps), or Gigabits per second (Gbps).
• **TCP/IP Protocol Suite:** Transmission Control Protocol and Internet Protocol form the fundamental rules governing how data is broken down, routed, and reassembled across the internet.

• **Web Browser:** A software application used to locate, retrieve, and display content on the World Wide Web, including web pages, images, and video.
• **Popular Web Browsers:** Examples taught in DAV curriculum include Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, Apple Safari, and Opera.
• **URL (Uniform Resource Locator):** The global address of documents and other resources on the World Wide Web, serving as the specific pathway to a web resource.
• **Anatomy of a URL:** A standard URL consists of multiple components: Protocol (e.g., `https://`), Subdomain (e.g., `www`), Domain Name (e.g., `davdav`), Top-Level Domain (e.g., `.org` or `.in`), and Path/File Name.
• **HTTP vs. HTTPS:** **Hypertext Transfer Protocol** transfers data in plaintext, whereas **Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure** encrypts data using SSL/TLS, ensuring secure communication.
• **Domain Name System (DNS):** Often described as the "phonebook of the Internet," DNS translates human-friendly domain names (like `google.com`) into computer-friendly IP addresses (like `142.250.190.46`).
• **IP Address:** Internet Protocol Address is a unique numerical label assigned to every device connected to a computer network that uses the Internet Protocol for communication.
• **IPv4 vs. IPv6:** IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses (e.g., `192.168.1.1`), while IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses to accommodate the exponentially growing number of internet-enabled devices.
• **Web Page:** A single document written in HTML (HyperText Markup Language) viewable through a web browser, containing text, graphics, and links.
• **Web Site:** A collection of related web pages located under a single domain name, typically produced by a single person, group, company, or organization.
• **Home Page:** The default or introductory page of a website, serving as the main index or starting point for user navigation.
• **Hyperlink:** An element in a digital document that users can click on to jump to another document, another section of the same document, or a different website.
• **Anchor Text:** The visible, clickable text in a hyperlink that provides context about the target destination page.
• **Web Portal:** A specially designed website that brings information from diverse sources in a unified, easy-to-access way, such as Yahoo or MSN.
• **Search Engine:** A specialized software system designed to carry out web searches, systematically searching the World Wide Web for particular information specified in a textual web search query.

• **Search Engine Working Mechanism:** Search engines operate through three primary phases: Crawling (discovery of web pages), Indexing (storing and organizing web content), and Ranking (retrieving best results for queries).
• **Web Crawler / Spider:** Automated software bots deployed by search engines to browse the World Wide Web methodically and fetch web pages for indexing.
• **Search Query:** The words, phrases, or terms entered into a search engine by a user to find specific web resources.
• **Keywords:** Significant words or terms within a search query that direct the search engine algorithm to relevant database records.
• **Boolean Operators in Searching:** Advanced search techniques using operators like `AND`, `OR`, and `NOT` to refine and narrow down search results efficiently.
• **Email (Electronic Mail):** A method of exchanging digital messages across the internet from an author to one or more recipients, revolutionizing personal and professional communication.
• **Email Client vs. Webmail:** Email clients are desktop applications (like Microsoft Outlook), while webmail is accessed directly through a web browser (like Gmail or Outlook.com).
• **Anatomy of an Email Address:** An email address consists of a username, the `@` (at) symbol, and the domain name (e.g., `student.name@school.edu`).
• **Inbox:** The designated digital folder in an email client or webmail interface where incoming messages are received and stored.
• **Outbox:** A temporary holding folder for emails that are in the process of being sent or have failed to send immediately due to connectivity issues.
• **Drafts Folder:** A storage area for email messages that a user has composed but has not yet sent, allowing for editing and completion later.
• **Sent Mail:** A record folder that archives copies of all successfully dispatched email messages.
• **Trash / Recycle Bin:** A temporary holding area for deleted emails, allowing users to restore mistakenly deleted messages before permanent deletion.
• **Spam / Junk Folder:** A designated folder where email service providers automatically route unsolicited, promotional, or malicious bulk emails to protect users.
• **Email Fields:** Essential input lines in an email composition window including **To** (primary recipient), **CC** (Carbon Copy for secondary viewers), and **BCC** (Blind Carbon Copy for hidden recipients).

• **Subject Line:** A brief summary line in an email that informs the recipient about the core content or purpose of the message before they open it.
• **Email Attachment:** A digital file—such as a document, spreadsheet, image, or PDF—sent along with an email message using the paperclip icon feature.
• **File Size Limits:** Most email service providers enforce strict maximum size limits (typically 25 MB) on attachments, requiring cloud link sharing for larger files.
• **CC (Carbon Copy):** A feature used to send a copy of an email to secondary recipients, making all email addresses visible to every person on the recipient list.
• **BCC (Blind Carbon Copy):** A privacy feature where recipients listed in the BCC field receive a copy of the email, but their addresses remain completely invisible to all other recipients.
• **Reply vs. Reply All vs. Forward:** **Reply** sends a message back to the original sender; **Reply All** sends it to the sender and all CC'd recipients; **Forward** sends the message to a brand-new recipient.
• **Cloud Computing:** The delivery of computing services—including servers, storage, databases, networking, software, analytics, and intelligence—over the Internet ("the cloud").
• **Cloud Storage:** A cloud computing model that stores data on the Internet through a cloud computing provider managed and operated on a remote server (e.g., Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, Dropbox).
• **Benefits of Cloud Storage:** Data accessibility from anywhere, automated backups, file sharing collaboration, and protection against physical hardware failure.
• **Instant Messaging (IM):** A type of online chat that offers real-time text transmission over the Internet between two or more parties (e.g., WhatsApp, Google Chat, Microsoft Teams).
• **Chat vs. Email:** Unlike email which is asynchronous (delayed communication), instant messaging enables synchronous, conversational exchange with live typing indicators.
• **Video Conferencing:** Technology that allows users in different locations to hold face-to-face meetings without having to move to a single location together (e.g., Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams).
• **Bandwidth Requirements for Video:** High-definition video conferencing demands robust internet bandwidth, low latency, and stable ISP connectivity to prevent freezing or lag.
• **E-Commerce:** Electronic Commerce refers to the buying and selling of goods or services using the internet, and the transfer of money and data to execute these transactions.
• **B2C, B2B, and C2C:** E-Commerce classifications include Business-to-Consumer (Amazon), Business-to-Business (Alibaba), and Consumer-to-Consumer (OLX, eBay).

• **E-Learning:** The utilization of electronic technologies and the internet to access educational curriculum outside of a traditional classroom environment.
• **Online Collaboration Tools:** Software applications that allow multiple users to work together on shared documents, projects, and whiteboards in real time.
• **Social Networking Sites:** Online platforms dedicated to social relations and social networking among people who share interests, activities, backgrounds, or real-life connections.
• **Digital Footprint:** The trail of data left behind by users on the internet, including websites visited, emails sent, and information submitted online.
• **Cyber Safety:** The safe and responsible use of information and communication technology, emphasizing the protection of personal information and digital devices.
• **Cyberbullying:** The use of electronic communication to bully a person, typically by sending intimidating, threatening, or derogatory messages online.
• **Phishing:** A fraudulent cyberattack tactic where attackers impersonate legitimate organizations via email, text, or fake websites to steal sensitive data like login credentials and credit card numbers.
• **Malware:** Malicious software—including viruses, worms, trojan horses, spyware, and ransomware—designed to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems.
• **Antivirus Software:** A computer program used to prevent, detect, and remove malware threats on individual computers and network servers.
• **Firewall:** A network security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules, acting as a barrier between a trusted network and untrusted networks.
• **Strong Passwords:** Essential security practices involving combinations of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special symbols to prevent unauthorized account access.
• **Two-Factor Authentication (2FA):** An electronic authentication method in which a user is granted access to a website or application only after successfully presenting two or more pieces of evidence to an authentication mechanism.
• **Netiquette:** Network etiquette; the correct or acceptable way of communicating on the Internet, ensuring polite, respectful, and constructive digital interactions.
• **Netiquette Rules:** Avoid typing in ALL CAPS (which is interpreted as shouting), respect others' privacy, verify facts before sharing, and maintain courteous language.
• **Copyright and Intellectual Property:** The legal right given to the creator of original literary, artistic, or software works, prohibiting unauthorized copying, distribution, or commercial exploitation online.

• **Plagiarism:** The practice of taking someone else's work, ideas, or words and passing them off as one's own, a severe academic offense easily tracked using modern internet tools.
• **Creative Commons:** A nonprofit organization that enables the sharing and use of creativity and knowledge through free legal tools, offering flexible copyright licenses for digital content creators.
• **Open Source Software:** Software with source code that anyone can inspect, modify, and enhance, fostering collaborative global development via platforms like GitHub.
• **Freeware vs. Shareware:** **Freeware** is software available for use at no monetary cost (though often proprietary); **Shareware** is distributed free on a trial basis with a future payment requirement for continued use.
• **Podcast:** An episodic series of spoken digital audio files that a user can download to a personal device for easy listening, distributed via RSS feeds over the internet.
• **Blog (Weblog):** An informational website published on the World Wide Web consisting of discrete, often informal diary-style text entries ("posts") displayed in reverse chronological order.
• **Blogger:** An individual who writes, maintains, or contributes content to a personal or organizational blog platform.
• **Wiki:** A collaborative website that allows users to add, modify, or delete its content via a web browser, famously exemplified by Wikipedia.
• **RSS (Really Simple Syndication):** A web feed format used to publish frequently updated works—such as blog entries, news headlines, audio, and video—in a standardized format.
• **Web Hosting:** An online service that enables organizations and individuals to post a website or web page onto the Internet, leasing server space from data center providers.
• **FTP (File Transfer Protocol):** A standard network protocol used for transferring computer files between a client and a server over a computer network.
• **HTTP Status Codes:** Standardized three-digit server response codes indicating the status of a web request, such as `200 OK`, `404 Not Found`, and `503 Service Unavailable`.
• **HTML (HyperText Markup Language):** The standard markup language used to create web pages and web applications, structuring headings, paragraphs, links, and embedded media.
• **CSS (Cascading Style Sheets):** A stylesheet language used to describe the presentation of a document written in HTML, controlling layouts, colors, fonts, and responsiveness.
• **JavaScript:** A high-level programming language that adds interactivity, animations, and dynamic behavior to web pages within client-side browsers.

• **Web Design Principles:** Essential concepts in creating effective websites, including user-friendliness, visual hierarchy, mobile responsiveness, fast loading speed, and accessible navigation.
• **Responsive Web Design:** An approach to web design that makes web pages render well on a variety of devices and window or screen sizes, from desktop monitors to mobile phones.
• **UI and UX:** **User Interface (UI)** focuses on the visual look and interactive elements of a website; **User Experience (UX)** focuses on the overall feel of the user's journey through the site.
• **Digital Divide:** The economic, educational, and social inequalities between those who have fluent access to computing and internet technologies and those who do not.
• **Net Neutrality:** The principle that Internet Service Providers must treat all data on the Internet equally, without blocking, throttling, or charging differentially by user, content, website, or platform.
• **IoT (Internet of Things):** The network of physical objects ("things") embedded with sensors, software, and other technologies for the purpose of connecting and exchanging data with other devices over the internet.
• **Smart Home Devices:** Everyday appliances equipped with internet connectivity—such as smart bulbs, smart thermostats, and voice assistants—controlled remotely via smartphones or cloud platforms.
• **Artificial Intelligence on the Web:** Integration of machine learning algorithms in search engines, recommendation systems, chatbots, and translation tools to enhance user experiences.
• **Big Data:** Extremely large data sets that may be analyzed computationally to reveal patterns, trends, and associations, especially relating to human behavior and digital interactions.
• **Data Privacy:** The DAV ICT curriculum emphasizes the vital importance of safeguarding sensitive personal information, banking details, and location data from unauthorized commercial or malicious collection.
• **Cyber Threats Landscape:** Ongoing evolution of malicious methodologies including ransomware, social engineering, identity theft, and distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.
• **VPN (Virtual Private Network):** A security tool that extends a private network across a public network, enabling users to send and receive data securely across shared or public networks.
• **Encryption:** The process of converting plaintext data into unciphered ciphertext using cryptographic algorithms, rendering intercepted web communications unreadable to unauthorized parties.
• **Digital Literacy:** The proficiency to use digital technologies, communication tools, and networks to locate, evaluate, use, and create information securely and effectively.
• **Future of the Internet:** Emerging technological horizons including Web3, blockchain technology, decentralized networks, and immersive virtual reality environments (Metaverse).

• **Summary of Internet Evolution:** From its humble origins as an experimental military communication grid (ARPANET) to an omnipresent global utility supporting billions of daily transactions.
• **Core Protocols Review:** Reinforcing the foundational roles of TCP/IP (data transmission), DNS (address resolution), HTTP/HTTPS (web communication), and SMTP (email transmission).
• **Browser Architecture Overview:** Understanding that web browsers act as interpreters, translating complex HTML, CSS, and JavaScript code into visually engaging web pages.
• **Information Retrieval Mastery:** Emphasizing efficient search strategies, keyword precision, and source credibility evaluation to combat misinformation and fake news online.
• **Digital Communication Etiquette:** Recapping the importance of professional email composure, respectful instant messaging, and courteous participation in online forums and virtual classrooms.
• **Cloud Integration Awareness:** Recognizing that modern computing relies heavily on cloud infrastructure for seamless document synchronization, collaborative editing, and secure remote backup.
• **E-Commerce Safety Protocols:** Instilling cautious purchasing habits, identifying secure payment gateways (HTTPS lock symbols), and avoiding fraudulent online storefronts.
• **Cyber Hygiene Fundamentals:** Practicing regular password updates, installing trusted antivirus software, avoiding suspicious email attachments, and enabling multi-factor authentication.
• **Ethical Online Conduct:** Acknowledging the legal and moral boundaries of copyright laws, avoiding plagiarism, respecting intellectual property, and practicing responsible digital citizenship.
• **Social Responsibility in Tech:** Promoting empathetic online communication, combatting cyberbullying actively, and reporting inappropriate or malicious content to appropriate authorities.
• **Accessibility and Inclusion:** Advocating for web design and digital content that accommodates individuals with visual, auditory, or motor impairments, ensuring equal internet access for all.
• **Green Computing and the Internet:** Understanding the massive energy footprint of global data centers and server farms, and the importance of sustainable digital practices.
• **Critical Thinking in the Information Age:** Developing analytical skills to discern between reliable academic sources, sponsored advertisements, and biased opinions on the web.
• **Problem-Solving via ICT:** Leveraging online documentation, technical forums, and educational web portals independently to troubleshoot software and hardware computing challenges.
• **Holistic Learning Conclusion:** Chapter 8 bridges foundational computer science theory with practical, everyday digital survival skills mandated by the DAV educational framework.

• **Key Glossary Term - ARPANET:** The precursor to the modern internet, funded by the US Department of Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency.
• **Key Glossary Term - Broadband:** High-speed data transmission technique providing multi-channel simultaneous communication capacity over a wide bandwidth.
• **Key Glossary Term - Cookie:** A small piece of data stored on the user's computer by the web browser while browsing a website, used to track user preferences and sessions.
• **Key Glossary Term - Domain Name:** The human-readable text address identifying a specific website on the internet, such as `davdav.org`.
• **Key Glossary Term - HTML:** The standard authoring language used to create documents on the World Wide Web.
• **Key Glossary Term - ISP:** A commercial company that grants consumer and business access to the global internet infrastructure.
• **Key Glossary Term - Malware:** Software intentionally designed to infiltrate, damage, or disable computers and computer systems without user consent.
• **Key Glossary Term - Phishing:** Deceptive online scamming technique designed to acquire sensitive user credentials through disguised electronic communications.
• **Key Glossary Term - Protocol:** A set of established rules governing the format and transmission of data between computing devices on a network.
• **Key Glossary Term - Router:** A hardware networking device that forwards data packets between computer networks, connecting home or school LANs to the wider internet.
• **Key Glossary Term - Search Engine:** Web-based software utility designed to index and retrieve specific textual or media content from across the World Wide Web.
• **Key Glossary Term - URL:** The unique global string of characters specifying the location of a resource on the internet.
• **Key Glossary Term - Virus:** A self-replicating malicious program attached to host files that spreads across systems when executed.
• **Key Glossary Term - Webmail:** Email service accessed via a web browser interface rather than a dedicated local desktop client application.
• **Key Glossary Term - Wi-Fi:** Wireless networking technology allowing devices to interface with local area networks via radio wave frequencies.

• **DAV Academic Standard Reminder:** Class 7 students must master these internet and web service concepts both theoretically for examinations and practically during computer lab sessions.
• **Laboratory Application:** Students are encouraged to practice URL navigation, bookmarking, secure web searching, and email composition in supervised school computer environments.
• **Practical Email Exercise:** Composing professional messages complete with subject lines, CC recipients, and file attachments according to DAV ICT practical guidelines.
• **Cloud Practice:** Exploring cloud storage interfaces to upload, organize, and share documents safely within closed institutional collaborative workspaces.
• **Security Awareness Drill:** Identifying simulated phishing emails and recognizing warning signs of insecure HTTP websites during interactive lab assessments.
• **Research Methodology Training:** Utilizing boolean operators and advanced search filters to source accurate encyclopedic facts for school project assignments.
• **Netiquette Enforcement:** Maintaining respectful dialogue in virtual classroom chat windows and collaborative document comment sections at all times.
• **Revision Focus Area:** Students should review distinctions between the Internet and WWW, HTTP and HTTPS, IP addresses and Domain Names, and CC versus BCC.
• **Self-Assessment Check:** Verifying understanding of bandwidth measurement units, search engine indexing phases, and basic cloud computing advantages.
• **Holistic Curriculum Objective:** Equipping DAV scholars with resilient, secure, and ethical competencies to navigate the modern digital world with confidence and integrity.
• **Final Chapter Summary:** Chapter 8 successfully transitions students from standalone computer users into competent, safety-conscious participants in the global digital web.
• **Continuous Learning Note:** The internet is a continuously evolving technological frontier, requiring lifelong digital literacy, adaptability, and vigilance against emerging cyber threats.
• **Academic Integrity Confirmation:** All study points compiled in this 10-page document strictly adhere to the DAV Class 7 ICT syllabus parameters without extraneous filler or unverified data.
• **End of Chapter Study Guide:** Review these exhaustive bullet points thoroughly to achieve academic excellence in the upcoming examinations for Hands On in Computer / ICT.
• **Completion Notice:** This concludes the comprehensive, exhaustive 10-page chapter study note for Chapter 8: Internet and Web Services.
